title: Subprocess with shell=True
description: Running a subprocess through the shell makes command injection likely if any part of the command string is influenced by input.
remediation: Pass arguments as a list with shell=False, and validate or allowlist any input that reaches the command.

title: Use of eval()
description: eval() executes arbitrary Python. If the input is reachable by users it is remote code execution.
remediation: Replace eval() with ast.literal_eval for data, or an explicit parser/dispatch table for behavior.

title: Deserialization with pickle
description: Unpickling attacker-controlled data is arbitrary code execution.
remediation: Use JSON or another data-only format for untrusted input; reserve pickle for trusted, integrity-checked local data.

title: Weak hash near password handling
description: MD5/SHA-1 used to hash passwords is trivially crackable at scale.
remediation: Use a password KDF: bcrypt, scrypt, or Argon2id, with a per-user salt.

title: SQL built by string interpolation
description: Building SQL with string interpolation or concatenation is the classic SQL injection pattern.
remediation: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements; never interpolate values into SQL text.

title: SQL built with Python % string formatting
description: Applying % formatting to a SQL string interpolates values before the driver sees them, which is SQL injection when any value is user-influenced.
remediation: Pass parameters separately (execute(query, params)) with the driver's placeholder style; never % or .format() values into SQL text.

title: innerHTML assignment
description: Assigning to innerHTML with data that includes user input is a DOM XSS sink.
remediation: Use textContent for plain text, or sanitize with a vetted library (e.g. DOMPurify) before writing HTML.

title: Shell exec with template literal
description: child_process.exec with a template literal usually means interpolated input reaches a shell.
remediation: Use execFile/spawn with an argument array, and allowlist any values that reach the command.

title: Debug mode enabled
description: Framework debug mode (e.g. Flask/Django) exposes stack traces and, for some frameworks, an interactive console.
remediation: Drive debug mode from an environment flag that defaults to off in production.
